nodes.summary: Given hash functions $h_1, h_2 : K \to \mathbb{N}$ and a number of slots $m > 0$, the $i$-th probe of a key $k$ is the slot $(h_1(k) + i \cdot h_2(k)) \bmod m$ in $\{0, \dots, m - 1\}$.
nodes.title: Double-hashing probe sequence

nodes.summary: The open-addressing table with $m$ slots and a given probe sequence in which every slot is empty.
nodes.title: Empty open-addressing table

nodes.summary: Given a table with $m$ slots and probe sequence $p$, a key $k$, a value $v$, a starting index $s$ and a budget $f$ of probes, examine the slots $p(k, s), p(k, s + 1), \dots$ in order, for at most $f$ probes. At the first examined slot that is empty or holds a binding for $k$, the scan returns the table with that slot overwritten by the binding $k \mapsto v$ and every other slot unchanged; if all $f$ examined slots…
nodes.title: Bounded insertion scan

nodes.summary: To insert the binding $k \mapsto v$ into a table with $m$ slots and probe sequence $p$, examine the slots $p(k, 0), p(k, 1), \dots, p(k, m - 1)$ in order. At the first one that is empty or already holds a binding for $k$, write $k \mapsto v$ there, leaving every other slot unchanged, and return the updated table. If all $m$ examined slots hold bindings for other keys, the insertion fails and returns no table.
nodes.title: Insertion into an open-addressing table

nodes.summary: Given a hash function $h : K \to \mathbb{N}$ and a number of slots $m > 0$, the $i$-th probe of a key $k$ is the slot $(h(k) + i) \bmod m$ in $\{0, \dots, m - 1\}$.
nodes.title: Linear-probing probe sequence

nodes.summary: Given a table with $m$ slots and probe sequence $p$, a key $k$, a starting index $s$ and a budget $f$ of probes, examine the slots $p(k, s), p(k, s + 1), \dots$ in order, for at most $f$ probes. The scan returns the value bound to $k$ in the first examined slot that holds a binding for $k$, and returns no value if it first reaches an empty slot or exhausts the budget.
nodes.title: Bounded lookup scan

nodes.summary: For every key $k$, looking up $k$ in the empty open-addressing table returns no value.
nodes.title: Lookup in the empty open-addressing table

nodes.summary: Let $T$ be an open-addressing table and $k$ a key such that no slot of $T$ stores a binding $k \mapsto v$ for any value $v$. Then looking up $k$ in $T$ returns no value. No validity assumption on $T$ is needed.
nodes.title: Lookup of an absent key fails

nodes.summary: Let $T$ be a valid open-addressing table, $k$ a key and $v$ a value. Then looking up $k$ in $T$ returns $v$ if and only if the binding $k \mapsto v$ is stored in some slot of $T$.
nodes.title: Lookup in a valid table returns exactly the stored binding

nodes.summary: Let $T$ be a valid open-addressing table and suppose inserting the binding $k \mapsto v$ into $T$ succeeds with result $T'$. Then for every key $k' \ne k$, looking up $k'$ in $T'$ gives the same result as looking up $k'$ in $T$.
nodes.title: Insertion does not affect lookups of other keys

nodes.summary: If inserting the binding $k \mapsto v$ into an open-addressing hash table $T$ succeeds and yields the table $T'$, then looking up $k$ in $T'$ returns $v$. No validity assumption on $T$ is needed.
nodes.title: Lookup after a successful open-addressing insertion

nodes.summary: Let $T$ be a valid open-addressing hash table and $k$ a key. Looking up $k$ in $T$ returns a value if and only if $T$ stores a binding $k \mapsto v$ for some value $v$.
nodes.title: Open-addressing lookup succeeds exactly on stored keys

nodes.summary: If a valid open-addressing hash table $T$ stores the binding $k \mapsto v$, then looking up $k$ in $T$ returns some value.
nodes.title: Valid open-addressing tables find every stored key

nodes.summary: Let $T$ be an open-addressing hash table with $m$ slots and probe sequence $p$, and let $k$ be a key. The lookup of $k$ in $T$ inspects the slots $p(k, 0), p(k, 1), \dots, p(k, m - 1)$ in this order. It returns the value $v$ of the first inspected slot that holds a pair $(k, v)$, and returns nothing if an empty slot is inspected first or if none of the $m$ inspected slots holds the key $k$.
nodes.title: Lookup in an open-addressing table

nodes.summary: Let $T$ be an open-addressing hash table with $m$ slots and probe sequence $p$. If inserting a binding $k \mapsto v$ into $T$ fails, then for every $i < m$ the slot $p(k, i)$ holds a pair $(k', v')$ with $k' \neq k$.
nodes.title: Failed open-addressing insertion finds every probed slot taken

nodes.summary: Let $K$ be a type of keys, $V$ a type of values, $m$ a natural number, and $p$ a probe sequence assigning to each key $k$ and each $i \in \mathbb{N}$ a slot $p(k, i) \in \{0, \dots, m - 1\}$. An open-addressing hash table with $m$ slots and probe sequence $p$ consists of $m$ slots, each either empty or holding a single pair $(k, v)$ with $k \in K$ and $v \in V$.
nodes.title: Open-addressing hash table

nodes.summary: Let $T$ be an open-addressing hash table, and suppose that inserting the binding $k \mapsto v$ into $T$ succeeds and yields the table $T'$. Then for every key $k' \neq k$ and every value $v'$, the table $T'$ stores $k' \mapsto v'$ if and only if $T$ stores $k' \mapsto v'$.
nodes.title: Open-addressing insertion leaves other keys' bindings unchanged

nodes.summary: If looking up a key $k$ in an open-addressing hash table $T$ returns the value $v$, then $T$ stores the binding $k \mapsto v$. No validity assumption is needed.
nodes.title: Open-addressing lookup returns only stored bindings

nodes.summary: If a valid open-addressing hash table $T$ stores both $k \mapsto v_1$ and $k \mapsto v_2$, then $v_1 = v_2$.
nodes.title: Bindings in a valid open-addressing table are unique

nodes.summary: An open-addressing hash table $T$ stores the binding $k \mapsto v$ when some slot of $T$ holds the pair $(k, v)$.
nodes.title: Stored binding in an open-addressing table

nodes.summary: For all types $K$ and $V$, every number of slots $m$ and every probe sequence $p$, which assigns to each key $k$ and each $i \in \mathbb{N}$ a slot $p(k, i) \in \{0, \dots, m - 1\}$, the empty table with $m$ slots and probe sequence $p$, in which every slot is vacant, is valid: it is probe-closed and no key is stored in two different slots.
nodes.title: The empty open-addressing table is valid

nodes.summary: Let $T$ be a valid table with $m$ slots and probe sequence $p$, whose keys have decidable equality. If inserting the binding $k \mapsto v$ into $T$ (adding it, or replacing the binding already stored for $k$) succeeds and returns the table $T'$, then $T'$ is valid: it is probe-closed and no key is stored in two different slots.
nodes.title: Insertion preserves validity of an open-addressing table

nodes.summary: Let $T$ be an open-addressing table with $m$ slots and probe sequence $p$, where $p(k, i) \in \{0, \dots, m - 1\}$ is the slot visited by the $i$-th probe of key $k$. Then $T$ is valid when it satisfies two conditions. Probe-closedness: whenever slot $j$ holds a binding $k \mapsto v$, there is an $i < m$ with $p(k, i) = j$ such that the slots $p(k, i')$ are occupied for all $i' < i$; this is what lets a lookup stop…
nodes.title: Valid open-addressing tables

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
